- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment = 1.00), especially in 30-day horizon; cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment was high 3–5 days prior.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model shows strong upward trend, true outcome often corrects downward within 7–10 days; adjust forecast slope downward by 10–20% if sentiment is mixed or declining.
- If sentiment history shows repeated high-low swings (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag true price movements; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead in direction of sentiment momentum.
- For long horizons (30d), model often fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment is volatile or extreme, reduce forecast smoothness and allow ±3% deviation from mean.
